title: Social media for nonprofits: 6 engagement tips | GoFundMe Pro

facts.fact: GoFundMe's Social State of Giving report found that each time an organizer shares their fundraiser online, it can help drive an additional $100 toward their goal.
facts.quote: we found that every time an organizer shares their fundraiser online, it can help drive an additional $100 toward their goal.

facts.fact: In GoFundMe's own survey data, 46% of Gen Z respondents said people should share their donations online to help spread the word and inspire others.
facts.quote: with 46% saying they believe people should share their donations online to help spread the word and inspire others

facts.fact: In GoFundMe's own data, half of Gen Z respondents said they share causes or fundraisers with their social networks at least once a week.
facts.quote: Half also said that they share causes or fundraisers with their social networks at least once a week.

facts.fact: According to Statista (third-party data cited by the page), TikTok had a per-post engagement rate of 3.7% in 2025.
facts.quote: 3.7% in 2025, compared to 0.48% for Instagram and 0.15% for Facebook.

facts.fact: According to the same Statista source cited by the page, Instagram's per-post engagement rate was 0.48%, compared with 0.15% for Facebook; the page does not state a year for these two figures.
facts.quote: 3.7% in 2025, compared to 0.48% for Instagram and 0.15% for Facebook.

facts.fact: The page states that X (formerly Twitter) posts that use hashtags see about twice the engagement of posts that do not.
facts.unit: x engagement vs. posts without hashtags
facts.quote: posts on X (formerly Twitter) that use hashtags see about twice the engagement of those that don't.

facts.fact: On Instagram, the carousel feature lets a single post include up to 20 images that users can scroll through.
facts.quote: use the carousel feature to add up to 20 images within a single post

facts.fact: The blog post was published on October 22, 2026.
